acceptanceCriteria: A repeatable script or make target reruns the per-test confined/unconfined comparison for declared packages and reports any outcome difference or skip increase.
Decide whether it runs periodically in CI (advisory) or before each declaration change; record the decision.
body:
V1-0246 verified .corvint/test-read-scopes.json once, in a Linux container: strace proposal, confined run, then per-test go test -json outcomes compared confined vs unconfined so a test that skips on a denied read is caught. Landlock confinement in full CI only catches a too-narrow declaration whose test fails; a test that tolerates a denied read (skips, or falls back) and a declaration grown broader than needed both stay invisible. Found 2026-10-01.

2026-10-01 (PR438) methodology finding: the first derivation ran in a tmpfs snapshot without .git and with GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false, so it never saw CI's conditions and missed that every confined nested go build fails VCS stamping. Any audit or re-derivation must run in a real clone with .git and CI's environment (GOFLAGS empty, GOPROXY=off, GOWORK=off, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, ideally -race -p 1). Re-run at 5e7dfab1 under those conditions: 99/99 identical, 5179 outcomes, 33 skips. Load-sensitive packages (internal/corpusindex, see V1-0587) need serial reruns before a confined/unconfined difference is attributed to the scope.
title: Audit test read-scope declarations: hidden skips and stale entries
